new_targets.observed_signal: Gogo acquired Satcom Direct in December 2024 and continues integrating the business. Its June 30, 2026 Form 10-Q states that a material weakness remains unremediated at Satcom Direct involving user access, segregation of duties and program change management over relevant IT systems, with additional work planned to migrate or enhance legacy systems and improve reliable information and segregation of duties. Gogo also reports acquisition/integration costs and business-aviation network/hardware/software integration risks. These are financial-reporting and integration signals, not proof of aviation-product or network-safety defects.
solution_wedge: OVERWATCH legacy-system migration and integration exception observability
AEROSHEPHERD bounded aircraft-connectivity configuration/installation evidence lineage
new_targets.notes: Very strong Boeing-like acquisition/integration control signal in aviation. No accounting, airworthiness, network-performance, installation-approval or remediation-effect claim is inherited.

new_targets.observed_signal: CECO completed its merger with Thermon on June 1, 2026 while continuing remediation of material weaknesses at Verantis, acquired in December 2024. CECO states Verantis was not appropriately integrated into its governance/control framework and lacked effective segregation-of-duties, certain IT controls and ongoing control evaluations. Management says it will focus on assessing and integrating IT controls at newly acquired entities. This supports a bounded acquisition-governance and industrial evidence-integration hypothesis, not a claim of product-quality or environmental-compliance failure.
solution_wedge: SARA acquisition governance and control-dependency evidence graph
PRE requirement/quality/compliance applicability mapping without certification claims
new_targets.notes: Direct public statement that an acquired entity was not appropriately integrated makes this one of the clearest marketplace analogs. Financial-reporting weakness is not evidence of industrial product or environmental compliance failure.

new_targets.organization: Mobix Labs / Vision Aerial / Special Project Delivery
new_targets.observed_signal: Mobix Labs is expanding a defense/aerospace electronics business through a National Security Matters initiative, including definitive agreements to acquire U.S. drone manufacturer Vision Aerial and Special Project Delivery, a critical-minerals/supply-chain platform. Mobix has also consolidated West Coast production in a larger military-approved facility. Its 2026 filings retain material weaknesses including IT program-change, user-access, computer-operations and program-development controls. The acquisition and control signals support a bounded integration/governance hypothesis, not a claim that Mobix defense products, drones or supply chains are unsafe or noncompliant.
solution_wedge: OVERWATCH defense-production and multi-acquisition integration observability
new_targets.notes: Strong national-security integration fit spanning electronics, drones and critical materials. Defense/export/CUI, product-performance and resource/reserve claims remain strictly external.

new_targets.observed_signal: Data I/O designs and manufactures programming and security-deployment systems for electronics manufacturers and is executing a strategic transformation including IT-infrastructure and operational-process modernization. This supports a bounded access/provenance/operational-transformation hypothesis, not a claim that its programming equipment or security-deployment products are defective.
new_targets.notes: Good electronics/manufacturing and secure-provisioning adjacency. Control weakness remains financial-reporting scoped until target-authorized operational evidence exists.
